These conditions are both classified under Myeloid Leukemia, and Ivosidenib is known to target mutations in the Npm1 gene, which are associated with t-AML-MDS. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of support for this relationship, with Quizartinib being indicated for a broader category of myeloid leukemia, which may include t-AML-MDS. The evidence suggests that Quizartinib could be repurposed for this condition, though the exact mechanism of action and the extent of its therapeutic effect remain to be fully elucidated. The pathways highlight the role of Ivosidenib in the treatment of myeloid leukemia, and the presence of a shared indication with t-AML-MDS implies a possible therapeutic overlap.
